prompt:
A line-art multi-panel storyboard of one continuous scene of a live-action short drama: one image divided into a grid of 3 columns and 2 rows of equal 9:16 panels, 5 panels read from left to right and top to bottom; cells after the last panel stay plain white. Every panel is a colouring-book drawing: contours only, in one thin uniform black line on white, most of the panel left white. Draw only the people and the few large shapes of the place (walls, doors, windows, a bed, a car). People are simple storyboard figures: hair is one smooth outline of its shape, like a cap, empty inside, with no strands, curls or waves; a face has one short line each for the eyes, brows, nose and mouth, and no stubble, wrinkles or jaw lines; a fence is its posts and top rail, a tree its outline. No texture, mesh, bricks, leaves or fabric folds; no shading, grey or solid black: dark hair, clothes and cars are outlines left white inside. Thin black panel borders, plain white gutters. Location: JI RAN'S OFFICE, Day, bright soft daylight through floor-to-ceiling windows.
Image 1: the character sheet of 纪然 (27), look S0
Image 2: the location JI RAN'S OFFICE, the front view, the establishing view, facing the back wall, with no people
Image 3: the location JI RAN'S OFFICE, the back view, turned 180 degrees, facing the front wall, with the left wall at its right edge, with no people
Image 4: the location JI RAN'S OFFICE, the left-side view, facing the left wall, with the back wall at its right edge, with no people
Image 5: the location JI RAN'S OFFICE, the right-side view, facing the right wall, with the back wall at its left edge, with no people
Image 6: the location JI RAN'S OFFICE, the floor plan seen from above: its top edge is the back wall, its bottom edge the front wall behind the front view's camera, and its left and right edges the left and right walls, with no people
Image 7: the blocking reference of this segment, the same place with its people in their places at the start; use it only for where each person is and which way they face, and keep each person on that seat or spot, on the same side of the room, in every panel until a shot moves them; do not copy its colours or light
Image 8: the prop coffee; use only structure, material, and color
Image 9: the prop pour-over coffee equipment; use only structure, material, and color
Draw each character so they can be told apart as in their reference image, by the shape of the hairstyle, the build and the outfit in outline only; never copy the photograph's detail. Use the character sheets only for the characters, not for their layout, white background or multiple views. Use the location images only for the layout of the space and the place of its furniture and props, drawn in outline. There is only one of each vehicle, piece of furniture and prop that the location shows, defined by the location images, throughout all panels; when a panel shows only part of one, such as a car's hood, it is that same object, and no second one appears. Each panel shows only the characters it names, and nobody appears twice in one panel.
At the start: Ji Ran stands behind the walnut desk, in front of the black leather executive chair, her back to the floor-to-ceiling windows and facing the office door. She holds the white coffee cup of black coffee near her lips. The pour-over set stands in the middle of the desk among the architectural plans, wood samples and one metal figurine. The camera is in front of the desk, on the office door side, and stays on that side.
Panel 1: Close-up, locked-off camera, eye-level, from the office door side. Ji Ran raises the white coffee cup to her lips and sips.
Panel 2: Medium shot, slow push in on Ji Ran from in front of the desk, eye-level. Ji Ran lowers the cup with her mouth closed, staring past the office door with the windows bright behind her.
Panel 3: Extreme close-up insert, high angle on the desk. Ji Ran sets the white coffee cup down hard beside the glass server, and the coffee ripples.
Panel 4: Medium close-up, low angle from the desk edge. Ji Ran's eyes narrow with her mouth closed, and her hand stays on the cup.
Panel 5: Close-up, slow push in to her eyes, eye-level. Ji Ran's gaze hardens into cold resolve, her mouth firmly closed.
Keep the characters, the number and position of every vehicle, piece of furniture and prop, and the location's spatial orientation consistent across all panels.
No text, letters, numbers, captions, speech bubbles, panel labels or watermark anywhere in the image; no photographic rendering.
